reuse.why: shared/schedules.ts already exports getScheduledAmount for exactly this resolution, but the diff never touches or calls it; each site gets its own inline version, and only getApproxNumberThreshold is reused.

duplication.why: The ranged/approximate resolution is written separately in api-models, schedule-template, forecast-schedules and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, with different rules at different sites.

placement.why: The amount rule is spread over the API mapper, the budget template, the forecast and the preview code instead of the shared schedules helper that owns it.

scope.why: The edits all concern the expected amount, though some appear to be leftovers of earlier steps that were never brought up to date.

maintainability.why: After four steps the sites disagree: the preview applies the lowest-value rule with approximate tolerance, template/forecast/API still use furthest-from-zero for ranges only, and schedules/app.ts posting/action sync and getScheduledAmount (UI) still use the midpoint.

bypasses_abstraction.where: api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal, budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList, forecast/forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions each resolve the amount inline instead of through getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: The same amount resolution reappears with different comparison forms (abs >=, num1 <= num2, approx threshold) across api-models.ts, schedule-template.ts, forecast-schedules.ts and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions.

abstraction_drift.where: The shared getScheduledAmount is left unchanged while api-models, schedule-template, forecast-schedules and the preview each re-implement the rule across the steps; the two schedules/app.ts sites (action sync, posting) keep their own midpoint copies.
